title: Exact ordinal and word-length matching retains edge association across lines, while within-line exact matching is inert
statement: Exact ordinal matching inside each original line is untestable: each (line,length,k) cell has one word, and no adjacent pair can move. A prospectively specified separate sensitivity therefore exchanges intact certain P words between lines on the same page, matching exact EVA-basic word length, exact original token-count width n and exact original index k. It preserves page inventory, per-position length and uncertainty barriers, but does not preserve individual line word inventories. The paired baseline uses identical cross-line cells except coarse initial/medial/final/singleton role replaces k. On the same34 previously used public practice evaluation pages, the original conditional edge MI is0.533009bits for ZL and0.512346 for IT. Exact-ordinal null means are0.444861 and0.414268, excess0.088148/0.098079, and both one-sided plus-one p-values are0.005 over199 draws.3229/4796pairs (67.3%) and3376/4740pairs (71.2%) can potentially move. Paired cross-line coarse-role baseline p is0.005 in both editions. The fixed default word-edge glyph chain also passes the exact-ordinal null in both editions (p0.005); independent unigram controls return p0.71 ZL and p0.015 IT, failing the preregistered0.01threshold, with IT near that boundary. One seed per control, no tuning. This shows persistence under a different cross-line null, not simultaneous control of exact ordinal and intact per-line inventory. It does not establish semantics, physical spacing or language. The original PR673 hidden fact remains unpublished and byte-identical.
check: Keep this cross-line sensitivity distinct from the previous within-line inventory-preserving null. No same-line exact-index permutation can test the claim because its cells are singleton. If registering a trusted ordinal null later, use page, exact token-count width, literal k and exact EVA-basic length, preserve barriers and each page inventory, and explicitly acknowledge changed line inventories. Require >=30 potentially movable adjacent pairs and a nonconstant null. Exact physical x/spacing needs independent image measurements. Control mechanisms explicitly modelling word-edge transitions can reproduce this association; one fixed unigram seed per edition is not type-I error calibration. Review and merge PR673 before any hidden fact submission; preserve the frozen original fact specification.

plan.question: Does edge association survive exact ordinal and length matching across lines on the same page?
plan.metric: Unchanged edge_length_cmi in certain literal adjacent P tokens; no promotion across uncertain or empty words.
plan.primary_null: Permute within (page, exact EVA-basic length, original line token count n, exact original word index k).
plan.paired_baseline: Permute within (page, exact EVA-basic length, original line token count n, coarse initial/medial/final/singleton role).
plan.tradeoff: Both new nulls allow exchanges between lines and do NOT preserve individual line inventories. They preserve each page inventory and positional length sequence. The exact-ordinal null is not a nested strengthening of the previous within-line null.
plan.impossible_null: Within (original line, exact length, exact ordinal k), every cell is a singleton: no permutation is possible. Report as undefined, never as a successful test.
plan.sample: The same34 public practice evaluation pages in ZL and IT; not new independent pages.
plan.decision: Require primary p<=.01 in both editions, >=30 potentially movable pairs and a nonconstant null. If not enough movement report undefined, never relax cells after results.
plan.limits: Exact transcription ordinal and token-count width, not physical x coordinates, glyph spacing, ink width or identical row composition. One fixed seed per generator.

evidence.selfcheck: Fixture passes: page, width, ordinal, EVA glyph length, metadata and barriers; real cross-line exchange; impossible within-line control is inert.
